What the status pills mean.
holds Reproduced, or never contradicted. Safe to quote.
partly overturned The measurement stands; a conclusion drawn from it does not. Quote the numbers, not the interpretation.
overturned The conclusion was wrong. Kept because the correction is itself the result.
superseded Correct at the time, replaced by a better-powered version. Output kept on /scratch, not deleted.
failed The job did not produce usable output. Listed because the failure mode is instructive.

21d · Unexecuted code, and excluded material

Compiled by walking the 43 Slurm logs, the slurm/ and src/ trees and the Nextflow history, rather than the write-ups. Both categories matter: the first because the notes sometimes cite them, the second because it is sitting in the repository.

ArtefactWhat it would have doneWhy it is listed
slurm/ec_rstar_pilot.slurm A 4-target pilot ladder (betaproteobacteria, firmicutes, euryarchaeota, vertebrata) at budget 500. No log exists. Superseded before launch by ec_rstar_fast (47292734), which used all 15 groups.
src/oracle_search/run_massive_grid.py A far larger Wasserstein grid: 3 seeds × 5 shifts × 4 base σ = 60 universes at n = 1,000,000, each subsampled over 13 ratios (780 rows). Never run; massive_wasserstein_grid.csv does not exist and there is no batch wrapper. Written, then abandoned when the oracle was removed.
src/adapt_adamw.py An AdamW variant of the adaptation loop. Dead code. Every batch script calls adapt_OGadam.py; only that one has ever been imported.
src/make_taxonomy_axis_{fig,noise,compare}.py Figures for the “is there one taxonomy axis?” question of Aug 4 §4. All three ran on 6 Aug, but no figure was committed and docs/figures/README.md does not list one. Either discarded or failed late.
src/plot_threshold_vs_realdistance.py The taxonomy ladder’s intended capstone figure: real r* against measured real distance, with the synthetic curve behind it. Ran on 14 Jul; no committed figure. The unified PNG exists only on /scratch.
archive/ is a different project and is deliberately not catalogued. Its files date from March 2026 (three months before this repository’s first commit), and every legacy config writes to /work/ah2lab/LiamK/plm-thesis-dynamics/results, a different repo. It holds five numbered legacy experiments plus their compile and plotting scripts. Two ideas from it are genuine intellectual ancestors and worth naming if asked: experiment 5 (“recovery threshold is dictated by the ratio of shift to source variance, not absolute shift”) is the direct parent of the base_sigma axis in the oracle grid, and its Wasserstein machinery reappears in the never-run run_massive_grid.py. No run in archive/ has a log, a result file, or an output path inside this project.
Two entries in this catalogue rest on notes rather than on a log. Job 47009884 (the estimation sweep) and job 47292611 have no log file in the repository. The estimation sweep’s output exists on /scratch and has been read, so the result stands; 47292611 has neither and is assumed never to have run.

21g · Provenance verification, by timestamp

Everything in this catalogue was checked a second time against file modification times on the cluster, rather than against the write-ups. This section records what that check found, because two attributions were wrong and one reassurance is worth stating explicitly.

Git history cannot date any of this work. The repository has seventeen commits, and every piece of pipeline code arrived in five bulk commits on 6 August at 19:16, followed by a reorganisation at 21:24. So commit dates say when the code was published, not when it was written or run. Every date below comes from filesystem modification times on /work and /scratch, cross-checked against Slurm log times.

The reassurance: generator v2 has not changed since it was fixed

FileLast modifiedConsequence
src/generate_synthetic_v2.py21 Jul, 17:02 Never edited since. It was not touched by the 6 August reorganisation, which did re-touch model.py, train.py and the plotting scripts.
src/run_distance_sweep_v2.py21 Jul, 16:51
src/calibrate_v2.py21 Jul, 15:53

That single fact settles the question this audit was run to answer. The surviving v2 sweep outputs were written at 17:23 to 17:28 on 21 July, and the two v2 datasets used for the realism scorecard were written on 6 August at 14:04 and 16:20. All of them postdate 17:02, and the generator did not change in between, so the August scorecard comparisons and the July sweep results describe the same generator.

What was produced before the fix, and is therefore not a result

OutputWrittenStatus
synth_v2_smoke/21 Jul, 16:32smoke test
synth_v2_flatcheck/21 Jul, 16:40 Its config has no target_sigma_inflate key at all, while every later config does. That is direct evidence the knob did not yet exist, and it dates the generator edit to between 16:40 and 17:02.
job 47136736log ends 21 Jul, 16:47 Ran before both the generator fix (17:02) and the sweep-driver edit (16:51). This is the run whose α-arm ceilings climb to 1.0000. Its outputs were overwritten by the rerun.
synth_v2_smoke2/21 Jul, 16:56smoke test
synth_v2_beta0.05/, 0.15/, 0.30/ 21 Jul, 16:59 to 17:01 Smoke tests, not the β arm, despite the similar name. Their configs record one seed, a single mixing fraction of 0.0, 3,000 source samples and 12 epochs. The real arm is the underscored synth_v2_beta_0.05/ and its siblings, written 17:25 to 17:27 with three seeds, eight mixing fractions and α = 1.0. There is no beta0.50/ directory, which is consistent with the smoke sequence being abandoned.
Nothing from before 17:02 is cited as a result anywhere in this document. The distinction matters because four of those directories carry the string v2 in their name and one of them carries beta, so a reader going to /scratch could easily read the wrong one.

Outputs that predate the last edit of the script that made them

Two exist. In both cases the output is the superseded one, so nothing downstream is affected, but it should be on the record.

OutputWrittenScriptScript edited
ec_swissprot/analysis/beta_diagnosis.json6 Aug, 16:07 src/beta_diagnosis.py6 Aug, 16:13
ec_rstar/rstar_allpairs_run1_superseded.json6 Aug, 22:33 src/ec_rstar_allpairs.py6 Aug, 22:35

The first matters for one specific comparison. The three-control β table quoted earlier comes entirely from beta_injection_matched.json (6 Aug 16:20, written after the 16:13 edit), so all three of its arms come from one code version and the comparison is internally consistent. The older file's isotropic arm gives slightly different numbers for the same condition (0.875 rather than 0.853 at β = 0), which is why the two are not mixed.

The v1 generator was edited after every v1 result

src/generate_synthetic_precomputed.py has mtime 21 July 14:39, while the last v1 sweep finished on 17 July. The edit is documented as a crash fix: a variable named perm shadowed the derangement of the same name, breaking the standalone command-line path. The sweep driver imports build_universe and sample directly and never runs that path, so the results are unaffected. The claim is checkable and it holds, but it does mean the code in the repository is not byte-identical to the code that produced the v1 numbers.

What could not be verified

ItemWhy not
src/measure_real_geometry.py, which produced the calibration targets Its mtime is 6 Aug 21:23, inside the reorganisation batch, so its July mtime is gone. There is no Slurm log for it either, so it was run interactively. The date the calibration targets were measured cannot be established from the filesystem. Only calibrate_v2.py (21 Jul 15:53) is datable, and it is downstream of the measurement.
ec_swissprot/analysis/scorecard_ladder.json mtime 6 Aug 14:10, with no Slurm log at that time. Another interactive run. Its numbers are quoted nowhere in this document.
The Aug 4 EC geometry and damage numbers They are dated correctly (4 Aug 23:03 to 23:07), but measure_ec_geometry.py and measure_ec_damage.py were both edited on 6 Aug at 13:59 and 14:00 and the Aug 4 outputs were never regenerated. They were produced by a version of those scripts that no longer exists.
Anything at mtime 6 Aug 19:13, 19:14 or 21:19 to 21:23 That is the bulk commit and the reorganisation. model.py, train.py, adapt_OGadam.py, measure_real_geometry.py and every plotting script carry those times. Their mtimes say nothing about when they last changed logically.
Everything else checks out. For the remaining runs, output mtimes fall inside their job's log window and after the last edit of the script that produced them. The four ladder arms are a good example: rstar_pair 23:56, rstar_matched 00:09, rstar_novelty 01:49, rstar_sizematched 02:22, with job 47292627's log closing at 02:22. That also confirms the sequencing described on the EC page: the 7 August write-up was committed at 00:00, when arm 2 had been running for four minutes, which is exactly why it records arms 3 and 4 as not started.

The two figures most likely to be misread, and why.
F10 is the only chart on this page that plots real and synthetic data on the same axes. It is deliberate (the comparison is the finding), but the toggle must be stated explicitly when the figure is presented, or it reads as one dataset.
F21 is a synthetic, family-labelled result that has been used to argue about α and adaptation cost. On real EC data α has no predictive power at all (ρ = +0.022, p = 0.87). The chart is not wrong; the sentence usually attached to it is.
